references.text: The introduction to the curses that will come upon Israel if they do not obey the Lord's voice, of which verse 46 is a part.
Describes how future generations and foreigners will see the destruction as a sign of God's judgment on Israel.
Isaiah and his children are set as a sign and wonder in Israel from the Lord, using the same phrasing as 'signs and wonders' (אות ומופת).
Isaiah is a sign and wonder against Egypt and Cush, with parallel use of 'signs and wonders'.
Israel will become a proverb and a sign among the nations, reflecting a similar theme of becoming a warning example.
Signs and wonders used to describe God's mighty deeds in Egypt, using the same Hebrew expression.
Signs and wonders mentioned in connection with God's deliverance of Israel from Egypt.
Nehemiah recalls the signs and wonders God performed against Pharaoh, using the same phrasing.
